_why: h-mad's five author agents did not require a line count + sha256 on the DONE line, and nothing told the orchestrator to gate on it. The protocol ran on five live dispatches (spec-author x1, design-author x2, implplan-author x1, plan-author x1) and matched five for five, but it lived only in hand-written dispatch prompts: measured at 6f00f8c, grep -ciE 'sha256|line-count|lines=' over the five agent files returned 0 for all five and SKILL.md held zero. The failure it closes: a subagent's 'stopped writing' is an INSTANT, not a state — the orchestrator's own post-DONE dispatch can make the author resume and write again, so the only durable proof is a digest the author computed and the orchestrator re-derives. Rows split across the gate's code and each of the six documents that carry half the contract, so a per-file regression cannot hide behind a sibling. Every row names its own `test` key: a battery scored on the whole suite lets a wrong-catcher pass as a kill.

mutations.name: the-sha-comparison-never-fires
mutations._mechanism: The gate's entire reason to exist. Every DONE line passes, including one whose digest describes a file the author overwrote after reporting it — which is exactly what a post-DONE dispatch produces.

mutations.name: any-string-counts-as-a-sha
mutations._mechanism: A truncated or placeholder digest reaches the byte compare and fails there with `sha_mismatch`, which names the wrong cause — the report was malformed, the file did not move.

mutations.name: a-missing-sha-field-falls-through
mutations._mechanism: The pre-fix DONE line — `version=v1.N` and nothing else — reads as a pass, so the whole contract is optional in practice while looking enforced.
mutations.find:
if not reported_sha:
        return f"DONEGATE: FAIL reason=no_sha_field path={reported_path}", 1

mutations.name: the-expected-path-is-never-compared
mutations._mechanism: The likelier mistake survives: an author that hashed the WRONG file reports a digest that verifies perfectly against the file it named, so every byte-level check passes and the wrong document is committed.

mutations.name: an-absent-artifact-becomes-a-cannot-judge
mutations._mechanism: Routes a refuted claim as the gate's own problem. The orchestrator goes to fix its inputs instead of re-asking the author, and `|| exit 1` does not fire on exit 2 the way a caller reading rc expects.

mutations.name: a-done-line-anywhere-in-the-message-counts
mutations._mechanism: Re-opens r17: four author reports were truncated before a trailing DONE and read as unfinished. A trailing DONE that survived truncation once proves nothing about the next report.

mutations.name: a-field-value-swallows-the-rest-of-the-line
mutations._mechanism: `path=` consumes `lines=` and `sha256=` too, so a malformed report becomes a confident wrong answer about a path that does not exist rather than a parse refusal.

mutations.name: the-line-count-stops-matching-wc
mutations._mechanism: The units trap, installed: `splitlines()` counts a final unterminated line that `wc -l` does not, so the gate and the author disagree on a file neither of them touched.

mutations.name: the-line-count-becomes-a-gate
mutations._mechanism: Turns the units trap into a build failure. A matching sha already proves the bytes are identical, so this refuses artifacts that are provably correct — the expensive direction of the same confusion.

mutations.name: an-unmeasured-line-count-reads-as-agreement
mutations._mechanism: `absent` and `ok` spell the same thing, so a DONE line that never carried `lines=` is indistinguishable from one whose count was checked and matched.

mutations.name: an-empty-message-becomes-a-refutation
mutations._mechanism: An empty message is a cannot-judge (rule 5's `empty $RP beside a DONE`). Reported as FAIL it sends the orchestrator to re-ask an author about a transport problem.

mutations.name: spec-author-loses-the-derivation-commands
mutations._mechanism: Without the exact commands the author picks its own — `md5`, a python one-liner, `gwc` — and the orchestrator re-derives with a different one, so a mismatch says nothing about whether the file moved.
mutations.replace: sha256=<compute a digest of the document>

mutations.name: plan-author-loses-the-fields-from-its-DONE-template
mutations._mechanism: The rule survives in prose while the TEMPLATE an author actually copies does not carry the fields — the same shape that let the REPORT= dispatch template be stripped while a bare `REPORT=` grep still passed.
mutations.find: PLAN-AUTHOR: DONE version=v1.N path=<the document you wrote> lines=N sha256=<64 hex>
mutations.test: tests/test_h_mad_done_gate.py::test_the_done_template_carries_the_three_fields[plan-author-PLAN-AUTHOR: DONE version=v1.N path=<the document you wrote> lines=N sha256=<64 hex>]

mutations.name: design-author-stops-saying-which-file-it-hashes
mutations._mechanism: The brief's open question re-opens: an author with `REPORT=<none>` has no report file, concludes the digest is unavailable, and drops it — when the DOCUMENT it hashes exists either way.
mutations.find: Hash the **document**, never your report file

mutations.name: implplan-author-stops-saying-lines-is-not-the-gate
mutations._mechanism: An author reads `lines=` as gating, hand-tunes it to whatever it believes the orchestrator wants, and a units disagreement that should be a note becomes a fabricated number.
mutations.find: `sha256=` is the gate; `lines=` is a cross-check

mutations.name: doc-auditor-hashes-the-document-it-audited
mutations._mechanism: The auditor reports someone else's state as its own: the audited document is not its deliverable and it did not write it, so the digest proves nothing about whether the REPORT is complete.
mutations.find: You hash the **report**, not the audited document

mutations.name: the-orchestrator-loses-rule-6
mutations._mechanism: Back to the measured state: five agent files require the digest and nothing consumes it. The author computes a sha, echoes it into the log, and the orchestrator commits without comparing — echoing is not a gate.
mutations.find: 6. **Re-derive the artifact's sha256 and refuse a mismatch, BEFORE you read `$RP` or commit.**
mutations.replace: 6. **Note the artifact's sha256 when the author reports one.**

mutations.name: the-rule-count-goes-stale-again
mutations._mechanism: The sentence introducing the list said `Four` beside five rules from the day rule 5 landed, and nothing pinned it. A reader who counts stops at rule 4 and never reaches the gate.
